children: Canada's main stock index pulled back from a four-week high on Thursday as weaker gold and copper prices weighed on mining stocks, while tech shares slipped on fresh concerns over AI spending following Meta's
quarterly results.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index

was down 0.8% at 36,032.84 points as of 10:13 a.m. ET. The benchmark had hit its highest level since September 22 on Wednesday after Canada unveiled a multi-billion support package for sectors hit hard by US tariffs.
Copper prices (HGc1) fell to a five-week low due to higher inventory, while gold prices
dropped over 2% on increased expectations for higher-for-longer US interest rates
The materials sector
, including metal miners, dropped 4.4% to its lowest since August 5
Tech stocks were impacted by fresh worries on AI spending after Meta introduced new non-voting shares on Wednesday to fund its costly expansion
Canadian tech stocks
declined 1.5%, with hardware solutions firm Celestica
falling 7.2%

"The market is starting to get concerned about the spending. Celestica is very much linked to the AI trade because of the work that they do for some of these hyperscaler companies," said Brian Madden, chief investment officer at First Avenue Investment Counsel

Brent crude prices rose 2.6% to their highest since May after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia heightened fears of a broader escalation in the Middle East conflict and prolonged disruption to crude supplies

"There is increasing chatter that the US and Israel may step up the campaign with more airstrikes after the US midterm elections in a couple of weeks. So it might be a case of things getting worse before they get better," added Madden
Energy stocks
slipped 1.3%
Canada's September producer prices increased 2%, compared with a 1.3% rise in August, amid higher energy and petroleum product prices
Logistics firm Mullen Group
rose 8% to the top of TSX after reporting quarterly results above estimates
